newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam radio told to guard against hostile forces.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam radio told to guard against hostile forces.

text.p: A senior member of Vietnam's Politburo has reminded Voice of Vietnam radio of its role as the Communist Party's information-age frontline against forces hostile to the regime.

The official daily Nhan Dan said on Friday that Politburo member Nguyen Duc Binh told employees of the official state radio organisation to improve their programmes and reporting style and safeguard the country's traditional identity.

"He also emphasized the important role of Voice of Vietnam radio on the political and ideological front...to stand against the frantic and crafty plots of hostile and reactionary forces," the official army newspaper Quan Doi Nhan Dan said.
Binh, director of the Ho Chi Minh National Political Institute, is in charge of party ideology. He is seen by Vietnam watchers as one of the Politburo's most hardline members.

Although faced with competition from radio stations broadcasting from abroad on short wave frequencies and now local radio stations on FM, Voice of Vietnam is still the country's leading mass medium in Vietnam.
Its audience is estimated to be more than 60 million, around 15 percent of the population, and it also broadcasts programmes in several foreign languages such as French and English.

Earlier this month another Politburo member, Lieutenant-general Le Kha Phieu, called for an overhaul of the state Vietnam News Agency to promote its role as the premier source of official information about Vietnam.
He said Hanoi could not monopolize information in Vietnam, but should seek to manage news as a means of competing with unsanctioned information from foreign news organisations.

"From hunting for news to reporting stories, we should be first, and cannot be behind," he said. "We should not allow any foreign newspapers or news agencies to usurp... the official voice of the Party and State."
